question: kit/07-QUALITY-BAR.md, R2, word for word
note: Each vote is one fresh agent that received one picture and the question of R2 and nothing else. The pictures carry neutral names; which judged frame each is stands in the key file, added when every answer is in.

votes.why: the cooled lava has conspicuously repeating swirl textures across the foreground.
the lava-plain ground has visibly tiled, repeating textures and the lava cracks glow flat, which looks like an ordinary hobbyist/stock CG landscape render rather than film-grade VFX
the flat emissive-masked lava plane and stiffly posed, repeated 3D creature models with weak lighting integration typical of an ordinary CGI render rather than a top-budget film.
the same swirled texture repeats across the foreground lava like tiles on a flat game surface.

the lava field has strong atmospheric depth and consistent, well-matched lighting, which looks like film or AAA concept-art quality. The odd creatures and the slightly smeared, low-detail texture on the plain keep it from a higher score, and (c) is the main alternative.
the mechanically repeating ridges across the foreground lava crust.
the repetitive procedural ripple texture on the lava plain and simple creature models look like a hobbyist Blender-style render rather than film-grade work

the procedural striped lava-crust shader and simple displaced terrain paired with offline depth-of-field and emissive lighting typical of an ordinary 3D render rather than a top-budget film or real-time web demo.
the foreground lava crust is made of sharply bounded patches with the same evenly spaced grooves.

The most influential thing was the lava-field ground, whose ropy ripple texture looks procedural and repetitive, and the stilt-legged creatures are low in detail. The depth of field and haze are good, but the whole image reads as a skilled solo or small-team 3D render, not top-budget cinematic work.
the lava’s flat emissive glow barely lights the surrounding rock.
the flat, repeating lava-rock ground textures and simple creature models look like an ordinary game-engine environment render rather than a polished film/cinematic frame
the flat ambient lighting and sparse mid-ground plane behind a detailed sculpted foreground asset
The lava looks like bright orange paint on the ground rather than molten rock casting light on its surroundings.

the lava field has convincing detailed textures, atmospheric haze, depth of field and glow, and the stilt-legged creatures fit a high-end game or film cinematic. The soft, slightly low-resolution background and the somewhat generic asset look keep (c) and (d) close behind.
the near-identical creature models repeated at different depths make the scene look like a staged 3D render.
polished but simple concept-art-style creature render (sparse scene, generic heavy DOF and fog, low-detail background cliff) reads as an artist's 3D render rather than film-grade VFX
the flat displaced ground plane with simple emissive lava cracks and identical reused creature meshes looks like an individual offline 3D render rather than a top-budget film or AAA cinematic
the foreground creature’s sharply faceted leg joints give its silhouette the look of a 3D model.
the creature design, atmospheric haze, depth of field and glowing lava lighting have the polish of a high-end cinematic or concept render, though it could also be a skilled solo artist's render (c).
the lava’s uniformly sharp glowing outlines make it look like an emissive 3D material.
the low-poly faceted rock on the lava slope and the simple tripod creatures look like an individual artist's Blender-style render, not film-level work.
the visible mesh seams and procedural rock-and-lava geometry around the cave mouth despite the cinematic lighting and alien silhouettes
the lava spreads across the foreground in thin, angular orange lines that look drawn onto the terrain.

The thin spidery creatures and the hand-built lava streams show it's CG, and the rock texture is somewhat procedural and stretched. The depth of field and haze are polished, but they look like a solo artist's render, not top-budget film quality.
